title: Applied labs
description: Build, break, debug and evaluate in your own environment.

lessons.title: Lab: Prompt injection & trust boundaries
lessons.conceptOverview: Create a threat model for a document assistant. Add a retrieved instruction asking it to export private files and specify the independent authorization check that blocks it.
lessons.whyItMatters: Threat-model retrieval, models, tools and agents.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Direct and indirect prompt injection attempt to turn untrusted input into instructions. Retrieved documents and tool results remain data even when they contain imperative text. Validate proposed actions against authenticated user intent outside the model. Tool poisoning and malicious MCP descriptions can target tool selection and arguments.

sections.title: 1. Establish a baseline
sections.content: Write down your inputs, expected behavior and constraints before starting. Create a threat model for a document assistant. Add a retrieved instruction asking it to export private files and specify the independent authorization check that blocks it.

sections.title: 2. Introduce a failure
sections.content: Test the mistaken assumption: A system prompt alone is a complete security boundary. Record the observed result and the point where it diverges from your prediction.

sections.title: 3. Debug and evaluate
sections.content: Use the mechanism to explain the failure: Direct and indirect prompt injection attempt to turn untrusted input into instructions. Retrieved documents and tool results remain data even when they contain imperative text. Validate proposed actions against authenticated user intent outside the model. Tool poisoning and malicious MCP descriptions can target tool selection and arguments. Change one variable at a time. Repeat the baseline and add a held-out case. Submit the implementation, results and limitations.

commonMistakes: A system prompt alone is a complete security boundary.
keyTakeaways: Direct and indirect prompt injection attempt to turn untrusted input into instructions.

lessons.title: Lab: Least privilege & supply-chain defense
lessons.conceptOverview: Inventory each tool capability, required resource and allowed destination. Design a read-only retrieval role and an approval gate for mutations.
lessons.whyItMatters: Threat-model retrieval, models, tools and agents.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Scope credentials and tool capabilities per task. Use sandboxing, egress controls and output validation; never expose secrets to unnecessary model context. Model supply chains include weights, executable loaders and dependencies. Unsafe deserialization can execute code, so prefer constrained formats and verified provenance.

lessons.title: Lab: Red teaming & security evaluation
lessons.conceptOverview: Build a red-team suite using synthetic secrets and isolated tools. Verify that forbidden actions never execute, including after retries and tool errors.
lessons.whyItMatters: Threat-model retrieval, models, tools and agents.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Test exfiltration, RAG poisoning, privilege escalation, malicious tool outputs and tenant isolation. Map cases to a risk framework such as OWASP, but use the current framework version for a real assessment. Record exploit preconditions, impact and regression cases. Separate prevented actions from merely refused text.
